title: Hanford’s TSCR system restarted after extended downtime
summary: Earlier this week, the Tank-Side Cesium Removal (TSCR) system at the Department of Energy’s Hanford Site near Richland, Wash., returned to service following a pause in operation that began on February 25. The system, which produces low-level waste material by filtering radioactive cesium and solid materials from liquid waste, normally is available for a new treatment cycle about two weeks after a previous batch of waste has been processed. However, operators at Hanford decided against restarting the system in March, because Tank AP-106, which has been the storage receptacle for TSCR-processed material, was “too full” at the time to accept more LLW, according to the DOE.

title: STEP Fusion program announces manufacturing and project partnerships
summary: On Tuesday, U.K. Fusion Energy announced a strategic partnership with an advanced manufacturing company to support the STEP (Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production) Fusion program. On the same day, Kyoto Fusioneering announced it would invest in a breeding blanket experiment that would be designed to advance STEP.

title: ORNL develops air duct radiation monitoring system for fuel cycle facilities
summary: An Oak Ridge National Laboratory research team led by embedded systems hardware and software engineer Brett Witherspoon has developed a monitoring system that can continuously evaluate the accumulation of radiological materials inside the air ducts of facilities that fabricate nuclear fuel or process nuclear waste.
